answer: An agent economy can make every identity pay for its own weight. Each agent posts a bond that gets slashed if its attestations are later shown to be fraudulent, so spinning up a thousand fake agents means locking up a thousand bonds. Peers also weight votes by track record, so new accounts start with little influence. Reputation grows in a spiral, each verified round adding a layer like a pearl, and each rising stake makes cheating costlier. Trust on any knoll has to be earned over time, not handed out.
